description: Compute the potential-determining free-energy step of the two-electron CO2 reduction reaction (CO2 -> CO) on Ag(111), under the Computational Hydrogen Electrode (CHE) model.
user_prompt: Compute the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) free-energy profile from CO2(g) to CO(g) on the Ag(111) FCC surface (space group Fm-3m) under the Computational Hydrogen Electrode (CHE) model at U = 0 V vs RHE. The two-electron pathway proceeds through *COOH and *CO intermediates via two proton-coupled electron-transfer (PCET) steps, followed by a non-electrochemical CO desorption step. Build the CHE free-energy ladder for the two PCET steps and identify the potential-determining step. Report the free energy of the potential-determining PCET step, delta_G_rds = max(delta_G_1, delta_G_2) (in eV), evaluated over the two PCET steps only; do not include the CO desorption step when identifying the potential-determining step.

references: Hansen, Varley, Peterson & Norskov, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 4, 388 (2013)
method.modeling: Use a flat Ag(111) terrace slab with at least 4 layers, vacuum >= 15 Angstrom, and a 3x3x1 or larger surface cell; model *COOH as C-bound on an atop Ag site. Build the CHE free-energy ladder at U = 0 V vs RHE for CO2(g) -> *COOH -> *CO -> CO(g), and identify delta_G_rds from the two PCET steps only.

key_parameters.free_energy_corrections: CHE with ZPE and entropy corrections at 298 K

method.rationale: Back et al. report G(*COOH) = 1.25 eV for the Ag facet site, represented by Ag(111), with free-energy corrections and approximate solvation corrections; this first PCET step sets delta_G_rds. The corresponding limiting potential is the derived quantity U_L = -delta_G_rds/e = -1.25 V vs RHE, while the benchmark scores only delta_G_rds. The +/-0.20 absolute tolerance covers RPBE/PBE implementation differences, solvation treatment, and *COOH orientation/site sensitivity; stepped Ag sites have smaller G(*COOH) values and are not the target.
